title: Exploratory analysis: distribution, correlation and outliers

videos.script: Somebody asks you for the average order last quarter. You write one query, and a number comes back. It goes into a slide. {{question}} Nothing in that sequence asked whether the table holds what its name says. Or whether a day is missing. Or whether one order in a thousand is a typo worth ten thousand reais. {{table}} This lesson is the hour you spend with a table before you trust it. You will build the shop this course studies, in a database on your own machine. Lantern Coffee, a roastery in São Paulo that sells online. {{shop}} Then you look at its orders the way an analyst does. First the shape of the values, before any average. {{histogram}} Then the extremes, at both ends. Some are mistakes, some are a different kind of customer, and one is the shop testing its own checkout. {{outliers}} Then a correlation that looks like a finding, and turns out to be two groups standing apart. {{clouds}} And last, the calendar, where one day has simply vanished. {{gap}} By the end you will have a list of what is wrong with these tables. Every number in the rest of the course is built on that list. {{end}}
